eli5.text: The program that helps manage certain software projects no longer works with older versions of its underlying platform, specifically, it now requires a newer baseline version that was released after the old one stopped getting updates. If you were running the project on the older platform, you'd need to upgrade to the newer version to keep things working. The system also swapped out an external helper library for one that's built directly into the newer platform version, so there's one fewer external piece to keep track of.

ai.title: Prompting tweak: ask clarification
ai.summary: Backend system prompt updated to require 3 numbered clarification questions for ambiguous requests. Instructions in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md` now emphasize minimal edits and concise responses. Scope limited to internal agent guidance logic.

eli5.text: The internal agent that helps build features has been updated to ask for clarification questions. When you make a request that could be interpreted in multiple ways, the agent will now respond with 3 numbered questions to better understand what you want before proceeding. Additionally, the agent's responses have been adjusted to be more concise, using minimal words while still conveying the same meaning. This change was made to improve the accuracy of the agent's understanding and reduce unnecessary back-and-forth communication.

ai.title: Checkpoint worker thread (91)
ai.summary: Checkpoint manager initialization moves to worker thread. `initializeCheckpointFileManager` now runs in `worker-script-project-context.ts` alongside file context loading, removing it from main thread startup in `index.ts`. `storeFileState` and `checkoutFileState` signatures updated to accept explicit `dir` and `gitdir` parameters, replacing module-level `projectDir` and `bareRepoPath` globals. `stageFilesIndividually` replaces `addFilesIndividually`, handling deleted files via `git.remove` and skipping unchanged files.

ai.title: Refactor checkpoint file staging to filter before async map
ai.summary: Checkpoint staging logic in `npm-app/src/checkpoint-file-manager.ts` moved status comparison into a synchronous `.filter()` step before the async `.map()`. This reduces the number of async functions spawned by `Promise.all`, processing only files with differing workdir/stage statuses. The change is internal to the core checkpoint manager, affecting no public APIs or user-facing surfaces.

eli5.text: The app's file-staging step now checks which files actually need updating before starting background tasks for them, so it no longer spawns busywork for files that haven't changed. This only affects the internal checkpoint manager, so you won't see any difference in what the app shows you or how it behaves. If you watched the app's background processing, you'd notice it starts fewer parallel tasks at once. The change is already live.

ai.title: Fix checkpoint manager git init and status filter
ai.summary: Refactored `initializeCheckpointFileManager` in `npm-app/src/checkpoint-file-manager.ts`. Removed early return on existing HEAD resolution and moved `git.init` into the catch block to ensure initialization only when the bare repo is missing. Corrected `stageFilesIndividually` status filter to use strict equality checks (`=== 0 || === 2`) instead of invalid `in` array syntax.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant and the notebook it uses to remember your conversation isn't already set up behind the scenes, it now reliably creates that notebook instead of sometimes skipping the step. The fix also makes the assistant check your changed files the right way, so it actually notices the edits you make rather than missing them because of a small comparison error.

ai.title: Add opt-out for clarification questions in main prompt
ai.summary: Updated system prompt logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to respect user instructions to skip the clarification step. Previously, the agent always requested 3 questions if ambiguity existed. Now, if the user specifies no questions, the agent makes best assumptions and proceeds. This internal change affects the core agent behavior.

eli5.text: The AI assistant can now follow your instruction to skip the follow-up questions it normally asks when your request is unclear. If you tell it not to ask questions, it will make its best guess and get to work right away instead of pausing to clarify. This behavior is part of the assistant's main instructions and is active today, so any request where you opt out of questions will be handled this way.

ai.title: CheckpointManager scopes git staging to tracked file paths
ai.summary: CheckpointManager now passes explicit `relativeFilepaths` to `storeFileState` and `restoreFileState`, derived from `getAllFilePaths` on the agent's file tree. Previously, `isomorphic-git` status checks scanned the entire project directory, risking performance degradation and unintended state changes in large repos. The refactor updates `checkpoint-file-manager.ts` signatures to accept object parameters and renames `restoreFileState` to `restoreCheckointFileState` in `checkpoints.ts`. Worker initialization in `worker-script-project-context.ts` now awaits file context generation before checkpoint setup to ensure accurate path lists.

eli5.text: When the assistant saves a checkpoint of your work or restores an earlier one, it now only looks at the specific files that are part of your project, rather than scanning every file in the wider folder. This keeps checkpoint saving and restoring more focused and prevents it from touching or checking unrelated files. If you watched your project folder during a checkpoint, you'd no longer see git briefly scanning files outside your project tree.

ai.title: Gemini fallback for lazy edits in fastRewrite
ai.summary: Added rewriteWithGemini fallback in backend/src/process-file-block.ts when promptRelaceAI returns lazy edits. fastRewrite now checks hasLazyEdit and calls promptGeminiWithFallbacks with geminiModels.gemini2flash if detected. Scope limited to backend file processing logic. Fallback preserves formatting and strips trailing markdown fences from the response.

eli5.text: When the system's first assistant came back with a lazy or incomplete edit, the editor now quietly switches to a second, more thorough assistant model instead of accepting the unfinished work. This only happens for internal backend file processing, so you won't see it in your app, but it means files that were previously edited poorly now get rewritten correctly behind the scenes.

ai.title: Checkpoint manager adds gitCommandIsAvailable helper
ai.summary: Checkpoint file manager switches to named `isomorphic-git` imports and adds `gitCommandIsAvailable`, which checks for a `git` binary via `execFileSync('which', ['git'])`. This supports using system git when available and falling back to isomorphic-git otherwise. `checkpoints.ts` updates `restoreFileState` arguments to `projectDir` and `bareRepoPath`, while `stageFilesIndividually` renames its local matrix to `currStatusMatrix` to avoid shadowing the imported `statusMatrix` function.

eli5.text: The assistant's checkpoint system now prefers using your computer's installed Git over its built-in fallback, only switching to the fallback when Git isn't found. This improves reliability and speed when Git is already available on your system. While testing this, you might notice smoother saving and restoring of your work progress, especially in projects using Git. The change is part of an internal update released on 2025-03-12.

ai.title: Refine ambiguity handling in main prompt
ai.summary: Updated ambiguity handling logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Changed condition from 'ANY ambiguity' to 'ambiguity ... preventing you from making progress'. Removed hardcoded limit of 3 questions, allowing variable number of questions formatted as numbered list if multiple.

eli5.text: The assistant used to ask exactly three questions whenever it detected any uncertainty in your request. Now it only asks questions when that uncertainty actually blocks it from making progress, and it can ask more or fewer than three depending on the situation. If you use the assistant today, you'll notice it interrupts you less often with questions and only does so when it genuinely can't move forward without clarification.
